ddx.step1_summary:
• Chief complaint: Painful, itchy, cracked, very dry skin on palms of both hands for 3–4 months.
• Symptom details: Began shortly after starting a new housekeeping job; worsened progressively and now ‘hurts a lot’ and forced 3 days off work. Occasional bleeding only after scratching. Itch intermittent. Mild generalized xerosis on legs. No fever, GI, GU, or systemic symptoms.
• Past medical history: Type 2 diabetes mellitus.
• Medications/Allergies: Metformin 500 mg (dose not specified). Tried OTC E45 emollient and an antihistamine without benefit. No known drug or other allergies.
• Family history: Diabetes; no known dermatologic, asthma, or bowel disease.
• Social history: Hotel housekeeper; frequent exposure to cleaning chemicals; often does not wear gloves. Non-smoker. Alcohol: ~2 pints beer/week.
• Vital signs / physical exam: None provided (tele-visit). Patient reports marked palmar dryness, fissuring, cracking; no spontaneous bleeding; occasional itch.
• Labs/Imaging: None mentioned.

V: Peripheral arterial insufficiency causing palmar xerosis: dry cracked skin can accompany poor perfusion, but no colour change or vascular symptoms reported.
I: Irritant contact dermatitis (chemical exposure): chronic chemical irritation from cleaning agents explains palmar fissuring, pain, itch, and temporal link to new job.
Allergic contact dermatitis (sensitisation to cleaning products/fragrances): pruritic hand dermatitis could arise from allergy to substances used at work.
Tinea manuum (dermatophyte infection): chronic scaling/peeling of hands can mimic eczema.
N: Squamous cell carcinoma in situ (Bowen disease) of the hand: chronic scaly lesion possible but usually focal, not bilateral.
D: Vitamin A or essential-fatty-acid deficiency causing xerosis and fissuring.
Diabetic neuropathic/anhidrotic skin changes leading to dryness and cracking.
I2: Chemical/irritant toxicity from cleaning agents (overlaps with irritant contact dermatitis).
Medication-induced xerosis (metformin rarely, but included for completeness).
C: Ichthyosis vulgaris—congenital tendency to generalized xerosis that can involve hands.
A: Atopic dermatitis (adult hand eczema): chronic itchy fissured hands in genetically predisposed individuals.
Psoriasis (palmoplantar): thick scaly painful fissures of palms.
T: Repeated mechanical trauma/friction from housekeeping tools leading to traumatic fissures.
E: Hypothyroidism causing xerosis (no other features noted).

step3_ranked_ddx.diagnosis: Irritant contact dermatitis of the hands
step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Classic presentation of hand dermatitis temporally related to frequent unprotected exposure to cleaning chemicals; pain, fissuring and dryness are typical for irritant (rather than allergic) process.
supporting_evidence: Onset shortly after starting housekeeping job with heavy chemical use
Primary location is palms (direct contact area)
Symptoms are dryness, fissures, pain > itch (common in irritant type)
No prior personal or family history of eczema/dermatitis
opposing_evidence: Some itch present (can still occur in irritant dermatitis)
Mild generalized leg dryness not fully explained by localized irritant exposure

step3_ranked_ddx.diagnosis: Allergic contact dermatitis to cleaning products
step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Sensitisation to fragrances, preservatives, or rubber components can cause itchy hand dermatitis; occupational setting is high-risk.
supporting_evidence: Occupational exposure to multiple potential allergens
Delayed onset (weeks–months) after new exposure compatible with sensitisation phase
opposing_evidence: Irritation symptoms (painful fissures) predominate over itch
No history of vesicular eruption or spreading beyond direct contact sites

step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Adult-onset hand-only eczema without flexural involvement is less typical, but xerosis and fissures fit eczematous process.
supporting_evidence: Generalized mild xerosis of legs suggests baseline dry skin tendency
opposing_evidence: No childhood or prior history of eczema/atopy
Lesions limited to palms rather than classic flexural sites
